answer.rationale: The hard constraint is no added delivery risk at 94% utilization with zero buffer, while still chasing the 18% spend cut. Incumbent renewal has previously kept integration and deliveries intact (c1); a primary cutover in 14 days would raise disruption risk even if the low-cost quote hits the mandate. c4 indicates benchmarking at renewal moved the incumbent on price and terms, so the competing quote should be used as leverage rather than as an automatic switch. Deferral is a poor fit because this contract does not auto-renew and the line is not non-critical. Verifying c4 (how much was actually recovered) and c2 (whether prior low-cost onboarding/delivery quality would even support a 14-day primary move) before locking the path. Uncertain that negotiation reaches a full 18% on its own.
